interpretation: Sample verified for two fresh-rootfs runs and eight fixed-input calls. Each call contains eleven interleaved eight-byte blocks. Independent Java XTEA with 32 rounds and the standard delta matches every native block using big-endian data and little-endian key words. The observed feedback is nonzero; subsequent blocks consume the preceding emitted block. Wrong data order, wrong key order, absent feedback and 31 rounds all fail on every block. The suffix is little-endian low32 of the INITIAL feedback buffer POINTER, not its contents or a verified checksum. VM ADD64_IMM16 reads virtual register 29 and produces register 21; the result equals the architectural store operand and initial feedback pointer. An eight-byte store supplies a four-byte copy, shared by the suffix and initial feedback prefix. Copies 9 and 10 assemble the eight-byte initial feedback. Its remaining source and key generation are not recovered. The final prefix is the first XTEA ciphertext byte XOR an observed VM immediate, narrowed to a byte. Neither the unchanged ciphertext byte nor the original pre-block byte is that prefix. Bytecode locations are the probe-recorded runtime cursors; they must not be universally equated with a current instruction address because handlers can advance their cursor before an observed store. Python receives observed pre-block bytes, key, feedback, feedback pointer and prefix immediate only through private pipes. Its 93-byte output matches the native constructor and AES data on every call. Complete prior seed, layout, field, constructor, writer, JNI, preimage/SHA-256 and AES controls are preserved. Shape counts are retained after discarding printable masks. Only relationships, lengths, code identities and final-field hashes are published. No raw keys, IVs, pointers, plaintext, scalar masks, signatures or operand digests are included. This reconstructs one stage from observed inputs; general inputs, Android equivalence, independent input generation, complete signer and online six-header acceptance remain unverified.
